_comment: Guided tour of the native FCS correlator workflow (also the FCS hub). Rail targets are matched by part of the step name; control targets are the step apps' item_rects. Every awaited step waits for the user to press the control.

steps.title: Five steps, in order
steps.text:
Correlation turns a photon stream into G(τ): how much more likely a second photon is at lag τ after a first one. The rail on the left is the order to work in: say which detectors are which channels, choose the files, optionally drop photons that are not from molecules, correlate, then screen and merge the curves.

The steps hand their results on by themselves; you only move forward.

steps.title: Start with data whose answer you know
steps.text: Example writes a simulated measurement: molecules crossing the focus in about 0.25 ms on a weak background, split over two detectors. Its curve must decay near half a millisecond. If it does not, the settings are wrong, not the sample.

steps.title: Only the ticked files are correlated
steps.text: Each file has a tick box. A folder adds every TTTR file in it. The two step switches below decide whether the photon filter and the merger are part of the run; a switched-off step is grey in the rail and Back / Next skip it.

steps.title: Which photons go into channel A and B
steps.text: Open the Correlator. An empty channel list means all detectors. For a cross-correlation that has no afterpulsing, put one detector in A and the other in B (the example routes to 0 and 1).

steps.title: Correlate
steps.text: Splits cut the stream into pieces that are correlated separately: their spread is your error bar, and a piece that looks different flags a problem in the measurement (a bubble, bleaching). The work runs in the background; Stop keeps the pieces already done.

steps.title: Screen and merge
steps.text: The FCS Merger receives the pieces. Untick the ones that do not belong, look at the merged curve, then save it or add it to ChiSurf for fitting.

await.hint: Select 5. FCS Merger on the left.
